- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.2) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates drop; add 1–2% buffer to forecast for next 3–5 days.  
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 20–40% in the 2nd half of the 30-day window.  
- Model consistently overpredicts mean reversion in 30-day horizon; apply 1–2% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.  
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating +/–0.4+), model tends to smooth too much; increase forecast variance by 5–10% in early days.
